summary: The provider factory is already lazy; the real boundary is the import graph rooted at `notify.__init__` and `notify.providers.base`, plus optional-dependency diagnostics and packaging metadata. The main risks are incorrect exception classification, provider-name resolution, runtime type-hint compatibility, and an incomplete extra/lockfile migration.

suggestions.title: Make the import graph the measurable acceptance boundary
suggestions.rationale: `notify.__init__` imports `ProviderType` and `Notify`; `notify.providers.base` then imports `notify.models` and `notify.templates`, which explains the observed `datamodel`/`jinja2` loading. `notify.providers.__init__` has no eager provider imports, so provider discovery itself should remain explicitly out of scope.

suggestions.title: Use a clean subprocess for startup assertions
suggestions.rationale: The existing template integration tests import `TemplateParser` and `TemplateEnv` at collection time and require careful `sys.modules` restoration. They cannot reliably prove cold-start absence. Add a subprocess test that imports `notify`, checks `sys.modules`, then verifies that first provider/template use loads the deferred modules.

suggestions.title: Treat Actor annotation resolution as a compatibility contract
suggestions.rationale: `Actor` is used in public `ProviderBase` annotations. `TYPE_CHECKING` plus future annotations prevents import-time failure, but `typing.get_type_hints()` will still fail if `Actor` is absent from the module globals. Either preserve runtime resolvability or explicitly test and document the changed introspection behavior.

suggestions.title: Replace capitalize-based class lookup with export-aware resolution
suggestions.rationale: `LoadProvider` calls `getattr(module, provider.capitalize())`, but `Notify("smtp")` currently fails because the package exports `SMTP`, not `Smtp`. Its ImportError fallback returns a module rather than a provider class. Resolve the class through the package export contract and add factory coverage for documented names and aliases such as `smtp`, `outlook`, and `ses`.

suggestions.title: Classify only genuine missing-SDK failures as extra errors
suggestions.rationale: The current broad `except ImportError` treats an unknown provider, a missing nested SDK, and a broken provider import identically, then retries through the dead fallback. Inspect `ModuleNotFoundError.name` or an equivalent import boundary so only the known missing dependency produces an install hint; preserve internal import failures and the original cause.

suggestions.title: Define extras by factory alias and dependency bundle
suggestions.rationale: A provider-to-extra map cannot safely key off class attributes: `Ses.provider` is `amazon_ses`, `Twilio.provider` is `sms`, while callers use `ses` and `twilio`. Several providers currently have no dedicated extra and only appear in `default` or `all`. Prefer a static alias-to-bundle mapping, validated against `pyproject.toml`, and decide explicitly whether missing dedicated extras should be added or reported through a group extra.

suggestions.title: Complete the dependency migration as a server-aware lockfile change
suggestions.rationale: `notify.server.client` and `notify.server.server` import `cloudpickle` directly, but the manifest has no explicit `server` extra; removing it from core can make server imports fail unless a server bundle is introduced. `uv.lock` currently still records `aiobotocore`, `cloudpickle`, `emoji`, and `pillow` as core dependencies, so changing only `pyproject.toml` leaves reproducible installs inconsistent.

suggestions.title: Add manifest and documentation parity checks
suggestions.rationale: The README lists providers but does not expose the optional extras, while the existing configuration tests already parse `pyproject.toml`. Extend that pattern to assert every documented bundle contains its required SDKs, moved dependencies remain available through `all` or `server`, and the README matrix matches the manifest.

suggestions.title: Make compiled-extension state part of the import benchmark contract
suggestions.rationale: `notify.exceptions` and `notify.types.typedefs` are Cython extensions, and `setup.py` controls their rebuild. A startup test run against stale or pure-Python artifacts can report a false import graph. Rebuild before the benchmark and run it under the repository's `filterwarnings = ["error", ...]` settings so the compatibility re-export is also proven warning-free.

suggestions.title: Ship the install-time breaking change with explicit migration notes
suggestions.rationale: Moving provider/server dependencies out of core changes behavior for users installing bare `async-notify`; the current README even states Python 3.8 while `pyproject.toml` requires Python 3.11. Document the exact extras and failure remediation in the README and changelog, including aliases and server installation.
